title: Anthropic's Claude can now orchestrate up to 1,000 AI agents in parallel through dynamic workflows
key_facts: Anthropic is adding dynamic workflows to Claude Managed Agents, bringing multi-agent orchestration to the platform.
A lead agent creates a plan, distributes tasks to sub-agents and merges the results; up to 1,000 agents can run in parallel per execution.
Anthropic hid 70 bugs in a 116,000-line codebase: a single agent caught 14 to 27 per run, the dynamic workflow consistently hit 66.
A senior OpenAI engineer recently called agent swarms a massive waste of tokens; The Decoder says whether the gains hold across task types remains to be seen.
Workflows are switched on with the "multiagent_20261001" agent type; Anthropic recommends starting small because they can burn through a lot of tokens.
quote_evidence: A lead agent creates a plan, distributes tasks to sub-agents, and merges the results when they're done.
The team hid 70 bugs in a 116,000-line codebase and found that a single agent caught between 14 and 27 per run, while the dynamic workflow consistently hit 66.
Whether those gains hold across different task types remains to be seen, so, as always, it's worth testing with your own workloads.
why_it_matters_hint: Businesses can split big jobs across many agents at once, but the speed and accuracy gains rest on Anthropic's own test and cost more usage.
notes: Short article; all performance figures are Anthropic's own.
